_status: PLACEHOLDER for the eval only. Drafted from common prenatal-exercise guidance (e.g. ACOG Committee Opinion 804). Replace with Noora's clinician-reviewed knowledge bank and get Niharika's sign-off before any real use.

approved_stretches.name: Shoulder rolls
approved_stretches.how: Sit or stand tall. Lift the shoulders up to the ears, roll them back and down.
approved_stretches.helps: Eases tightness in the neck and upper back.

approved_stretches.name: Seated side stretch
approved_stretches.how: Sit on a chair or the floor. Raise one arm overhead and lean gently to the other side. Switch sides.
approved_stretches.helps: Eases tightness along the sides of the body.

approved_stretches.name: Ankle circles
approved_stretches.how: Sit with feet off the floor or on a low stool. Turn each foot slowly in circles both ways.
approved_stretches.helps: Helps blood flow in the legs and can ease foot swelling.

approved_stretches.name: Cat-cow (hands-and-knees back stretch)
approved_stretches.how: On hands and knees. Breathe in and let the belly drop gently; breathe out and round the back up.

approved_stretches.name: Wall calf stretch
approved_stretches.how: Hands on a wall, one foot back with heel down, lean forward until the back calf feels a gentle stretch.
approved_stretches.helps: Eases calf tightness and leg cramps.

approved_stretches.name: Seated butterfly
approved_stretches.how: Sit on the floor, soles of the feet together, knees out. Sit tall and let the knees drop gently. Do not push the knees down.

approved_stretches.name: Standing pelvic tilt against a wall
approved_stretches.how: Stand with back against a wall, knees soft. Gently press the lower back toward the wall, then release.
approved_stretches.helps: Eases lower back ache as the belly grows.

contraindicated_elements: lying flat on the back after the first trimester
stretching until it hurts or to the very end of the range
positions where she could lose balance and fall, without support
